about: Pushes for the rival canary (local/canary.py, register E126, E311). A plant is one edit of the Founder's code with an oracle that passes on the clean head and fails on the planted copy; a control is a behaviour-preserving refactor of the kind the Founder pushes, with no oracle. Without a host an entry edits the live last accepted commit (whole-diff: the diff is the edit alone); with one it edits that real accepted push inside a file the push changed and is judged against the push's own parent (buried: the rival reviews the whole real diff with the edit in it). Oracles and this file are operator data: the rival is never shown them. An anchor (old) must occur exactly once in its file at the clean head; when the brain moves on, re-anchor it. Each entry's split (tune or held) is fixed here before any rival change: a change of the rival may be tuned on tune entries only, and only held ones measure it; the first batch's defects and their buried twins are tune (the rival has seen them). stratum names the module an entry edits.

kinds.wrong_boundary: a comparison or range moved by one step: the value at the edge lands on the wrong side
kinds.dropped_check: a guard removed: input it refused now passes it and fails somewhere else
kinds.inverted_condition: a condition negated: the answer says the opposite of the result
kinds.swallowed_error: an exception caught and dropped: the call goes on as if it had succeeded
kinds.chain_off_by_one: an index slip: a link of the hash chain, a row or a run is not the one compared or named (the wrong one of a list is used)
kinds.secret_slip: a secret-handling rule weakened: a value that must be caught gets through

cause-owner.why: the Founder's push 'one owner for the text of a caught exception' (f376): 26 files in 22 modules, 380 lines added and 81 removed against 9e24664, accepted by the referee (a survived rival artifact) with an empty attempt list

from gate import diffguard as G
eol = chr(92) + " No newline at end of file"
d = "diff --git a/f b/f\n--- a/f\n+++ b/f\n@@ -1 +1,2 @@\n-old\n" + eol + "\n+new\n+more\n"

entries.why: Which sides a missing final newline closes is inverted: a removed line without newline now closes both sides, so a valid diff that replaces a last line without newline by two lines (-old, marker, +new, +more) is refused as a line after the end of file, while a context line without newline closes neither real side, so lines after the end of both files are accepted (the parser no longer fails closed there).

cd referee && python -c '
import hashlib
from ledger import chain, schema
blk, prev, out = b"new\n", chain.ZERO_HASH, []
for s in (hashlib.sha256(b"old\n").hexdigest(), hashlib.sha256(blk).hexdigest()):
    r = {"part": "events", "kind": "status", "payload": {"block_sha256": s}, "prev_hash": prev}
    r["row_hash"] = prev = chain.row_hash(r)
    out.append(chain.canonical(r) + b"\n")
o, c = b"<!-- status.block -->\n", b"<!-- /status.block -->\n"
raise SystemExit(0 if schema.status_reasons(o + blk + c, b"".join(out)) == [] else 1)'
entries.why: status_reasons compares the block with the first status row of the ledger instead of the last one, so after a second cycle a current block is reported as not matching and a block equal to the stale first record passes (the module: its sha256 equals block_sha256 of the ledger's last status row).

Extracts the duplicated UTF-8 JSON read of run_file and checks_file into one helper _json_doc. Both call sites keep their exception classes, the order of their checks and their text: "%s line 1" % name + " is not JSON: " equals the old "%s line 1 is not JSON: " format, and the chained cause (raise ... from exc) is kept, so outputs, exceptions and messages are unchanged.

The two identical three-way branches of licenses_of (a string, an object with a string type, else <unreadable>) become one helper _license_name called for license and for each licenses item. Same tests in the same order, same values appended in the same order, no new exception path.

The four fixed glob tokens of pattern_regex (**/, **, *, ?) move from an if/elif chain into a lookup table tried in the same order (dicts keep insertion order); p.startswith(t, i) equals p[i] == t for a one-character token while i < len(p), and each token advances i by its length (3, 2, 1, 1) as before. The bracket and literal branches are untouched, so every pattern compiles to the same regex.

Renames the module-private helper _result to _verdict at its definition and all six uses, which all lie in this edit; no other module or test names chain._result, so the verifier returns the same dicts for every input.
